rows.note: Use 工作 as the all-purpose noun for a job or for tasks that need doing.

example.english: I have a lot of work to do today.
example.traditional: 我今日有好多工作要做。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 jau5 hou2 do1 gung1 zok3 jiu3 zou6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice for doing a task or working.

example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 jiu3 zou6 je5

rows.note: Use 公司 for the company as the workplace or as the employer, especially in office-work contexts.

example.english: I work at a company in Kwun Tong.
example.jyutping: ngo5 hai2 gun1 tong4 gaan1 gung1 si1 faan1 gung1

rows.note: Use 功夫 for the effort or labour put into accomplishing a particular task.

example.english: We put a lot of work into this report.
example.traditional: 呢份報告落咗好多功夫。
example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 bou3 gou3 lok6 zo2 hou2 do1 gung1 fu1

rows.note: Use 運作 when something functions or operates in a particular way.

example.english: This machine can work very smoothly.
example.jyutping: ni1 bou6 gei1 wan6 zok3 dak1 hou2 seon6

rows.note: Use 操作 when setting a machine, control, or mechanism into action by handling it.

example.english: Do you know how to work this machine?
example.jyutping: nei5 sik1 m4 sik1 cou1 zok3 ni1 bou6 gei1

rows.note: Use 啱 when something suits someone or is appealing to them.

example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 gung1 zan1 hai6 hou2 ngaam1 ngo5

rows.note: Use 作品 for a literary, artistic, or intellectual work as a finished creation.

example.english: This novel is their finest work.
example.traditional: 呢套小說係佢最出色嘅作品。
example.jyutping: ni1 tou3 siu2 syut3 hai6 keoi5 zeoi3 ceot1 sik1 ge3 zok3 ban2
